item.title: Border health: 120 euros per month for medical salaries
item.description: Lombardy applies the contribution from 3% to 6%: funds to border doctors to curb the flight to Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## Briefly - A 20% increase in salaries for doctors and nurses within 20 km of the border. - Measure financed by contribution of old frontiersmen from 3% to 6% net. - A frontiersman earning 4,000 Swiss francs net will pay around 120 euros per month for the SSN. - **What**: Health contribution borne by old frontiersmen and 20% incentive for border healthcare workers - When: Second half of April 2026 - Where: Border area within twenty kilometers from Switzerland and Lombardy region - Who: Regional Councillor Massimo Sertori, Lombardy Region, healthcare employers - Amount: From 30 to 200 euros per month at the expense of frontiersmen; 20% bonus for doctors (around 10,000 euros per year) and nurses (5,400 euros per year) ### The Lombardy plan to value healthcare personnel In April 2026, the operational details are defined to counter the emigration of Italian healthcare personnel attracted by Swiss salaries. The Lombardy Region aims to increase salaries of doctors and nurses working in public structures within a radius of twenty kilometers from the Swiss border by 20%. The measure aims to make Italian border hospitals attractive, where professionals are increasingly difficult to engage due to salaries across the border that are three or four times higher than those in Italy. ### How much does the contribution collect from frontiersmen Translated into concrete figures, the provision translates into a retributive increase of around ten thousand euros per year for each doctor and 5,400 euros per year for each nurse in service in the border area. The financing of this measure, not burdening central coffers, is guaranteed by a contribution requested from workers residing in Italy employed in Switzerland under the discipline of old frontiersmen. For a worker earning the equivalent of four thousand Swiss francs net per month, the rate involves a deduction of around 120 euros per month in favour of the National Health Service. The provision is defended by Regional Councillor Massimo Sertori, who reiterates the goodness of the regional choice of applying the contribution starting from the minimum percentage of 3%, even in the presence of a state law that allows going up to 6% of net income. To verify how these withholdings impact on the overall salary before claiming the [salary calculator](nav:calculator), it is essential to carefully analyse the differences between gross and net income produced by the application of the tax system. ### The historical roots of the old frontier regime
To understand the reasons for the measure, it is necessary to retrace the history of the tax and health treatment reserved for those who reside in Italy and work abroad. Those who have held the G permit since before July 2023 fall under the transitional regime and benefit from the historical mechanism of exclusive cross-border taxation. For 27 years the old frontier workers have benefited from the benefits of the Italian National Health Service together with their family members, while paying the tax at source exclusively to the Swiss authorities and without having to pay income taxes to the Italian Revenue Agency.
Until 1999, commuters paid sick pay in Switzerland for their own personal coverage and paid a bill of about 600 thousand lire to guarantee assistance to their family members in Italy. With the transition of health management to the Regions and the introduction of the agreement between Switzerland and the European Union on the right of option, the framework has changed. Each border worker had the right to choose within three months of hiring whether to subscribe to the Swiss LAMal coverage (with premiums starting from about 350 euros per month for the individual worker) or rely on the Italian SSN. However, due to a prolonged regulatory vacuum, the old border workers did not pay additional fees for Italian health care while maintaining its full coverage.

item.title: Temporary work in Switzerland continues to grow
item.description: Temporary working hours increased by 1.5% in the first half, while permanent contracts fell by 19.4%.
item.content:encoded:
## Briefly, - Temporary work hours increase by 1.5% in the first half of the year. - Permanent placements decrease by 19.4%. - 79% of agencies already use artificial intelligence.
## Key facts - **What**: Increase in temporary work - When: First half of the year (compared to the previous year) - Where: Switzerland, Swissstaffing data - Who: Swissstaffing, CEO of associated agencies - Amount: +1.5% temporary hours, -19.4% permanent, 79% AI, 33% growth forecast
### Swissstaffing report data Swissstaffing, the recruitment agency association, published the first half data on Wednesday. Temporary workers' hours increased by 1.5% compared to the same period last year, a sign of a rebound after three years of declines. At the same time, permanent placements fell by 19.4%, reflecting the uncertainty of the Swiss economy.
Marius Osterfeld, Swissstaffing's chief economist, explained that Swiss industrial production showed a positive trend at the beginning of the year, despite the slowdown in the Iran war. This generated an increase in demand for temporary work in the industrial sector and a 'slight increase in working hours'.
The introduction of artificial intelligence is one of the main novelties: 79% of respondents claim to already use AI, especially to increase efficiency and improve recruitment processes. Furthermore, the surplus of candidates (in some cases over 100 for a position) makes AI a crucial tool for selection.
Finally, 33% of CEOs of Swissstaffing-affiliated companies expect an increase in activity in the next six months, provided that geopolitical events do not worsen further. These data provide a clear picture of the temporary work market, a segment that directly affects the border workers of the Canton Ticino, who often resort to term contracts to cover peaks in demand.

### Implications for Ticino border workers The increase in temporary work hours has concrete repercussions for Ticino border workers. A 1.5% increase in hours worked indicates a greater availability of job openings, especially in industrial sectors that have benefited from increased production. For those already in possession of a **G permit**, this can translate into a wider range of job opportunities, reducing dependence on indefinite contracts, which currently show a decline of 19.4%.
From a tax perspective, border workers continue to pay source tax only in Switzerland, as established by the 1976 Double Taxation Convention. The new tax agreement, effective January 1, 2024, confirms this method, avoiding double taxation. Therefore, the increase in temporary contracts does not immediately affect the tax burden, but requires proper management of the pay slip, with the related AVS (5.3% for the employee) and LPP (7-18% depending on age) deductions.
The widespread use of AI (79% of agencies) changes the way job applications are evaluated. Border workers who present a digital CV must ensure that their data is structured in a clear manner, as selection algorithms favor easily readable information. A candidate can receive more than 100 requests for a single position; the ability to stand out becomes crucial.
One-third of CEOs expects further growth in the next six months, suggesting that demand for temporary work may continue to rise, but this depends on geopolitical developments. For border workers, this implies the need to constantly monitor job offers on work platforms and maintain up-to-date professional profiles.

## In a nutshell - The employer's registered office may be outside the border area - Counts the physical place where the work is performed - Basic requirement: residence within 20 km of the border - The limits for teleworking set at 25% per year have been confirmed
## Key facts - **What**: Answer question no. 126/2026 Revenue Agency - When: Enforcement of post-Agreement 2020 legislation - Where: Border area (Lombardy, Piedmont, Ticino, Graubünden) - Who: Scientific informant resident in Ticino - Amount: Deductible of 10,000 euros for new frontier workers
The Revenue Agency has dissolved an interpretative knot that burdened thousands of cross-border workers through the answer to call no. 126/2026. The case under consideration concerns a worker residing in a Swiss border municipality in the Canton of Ticino, employed as a scientific informant of the drug. The professional operates entirely in Lombardy, therefore within 20 km of the Swiss border, but on behalf of a company that has its registered office in Veneto, a region totally unrelated to the map of border areas. The central question was whether the geographical location of the employer's administrative headquarters could preclude access to the preferential tax regime provided for by the New Agreement between Italy and Switzerland.
### The primacy of physical performance
The Tax Office has determined that the tax status of the worker is governed by ## Old and new border crossers: the differences in the withdrawal
The Revenue Agency's clarification fits into a tax system now divided into two distinct tracks. The so-called old frontier workers are those who worked in Switzerland for at least one day between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023. For this category, the agreement guarantees the maintenance of the exclusive taxation regime at source in Switzerland, with a total IRPEF exemption in Italy. This right remains valid even in the event of a change of employer, provided that the interruption of the relationship does not exceed 12 months and that the new employment remains in the border area.
### The New Hire Mechanism
For those who started the business from 18 July 2023, the situation changes radically towards a competing taxation model. In this scenario, Switzerland applies a reduced source tax, equal to 80% of the ordinary tax calculated according to the cantonal tables. The worker is then required to present the [dichiarazione dei redditi](nav:tax-return) in Italy. Here, the entire income is subject to IRPEF taxation, but with specific mitigation mechanisms: an exemption deductible of 10,000 euros and the full deductibility of Swiss mandatory social security contributions, such as [AVS](nav:pension) and [LPP](nav:pension). To avoid double taxation, a tax credit is recognized for what has already been paid to the Swiss authorities.
A critical aspect concerns the management of the smart ## Procedures and checks for the worker
To benefit correctly from the tax regime, the worker must ensure that their contractual and logistical situation complies with the parameters defined by interpello 126/2026. The first step is to verify the kilometric distance between the municipality of residence and the border, which must be less than or equal to 20 km. Subsequently, it is necessary for the employment contract or a statement from the employer to clearly specify that the performance takes place within the border area, regardless of where the company's legal headquarters is located. This document is essential in case of checks by Italian tax authorities.
### Declaration obligations and deadlines
New border workers must pay particular attention to the completion of specific tables in the Redditi or 730 model. It is necessary to report the Swiss gross income, deduct pension contributions and apply the €10,000 exemption. The calculation of the tax credit requires proof of payments made in Switzerland for income tax at source. Even old border workers, although enjoying exemption, must monitor any changes in their situation, such as exceeding the 12-month inactivity limit that could make them lose the transitional regime of favor.
The tax authority's decision represents a revolution for Italian companies located far from the border that intend to take advantage of professionals residing in Switzerland. The possibility of correctly classifying these workers as border workers, even with headquarters in Venice or Rome, opens up new recruitment opportunities without creating tax uncertainty for the employee. It is recommended to always keep copies of residence certificates and time sheets that attest to physical presence in the border area, especially for itinerant professions such as scientific informants. Compliance with the requirements for daily commuting remains an indispensable pillar for maintaining access to the tax benefits provided by the Italian-Swiss order.

The data show that independent chains tend to modify prices almost simultaneously and with identical amounts, as highlighted by a case in Pfäffikon from February 2022 to October 2023. item.title: Cross-border commuters: Ticino applies the full withholding rate
item.description: Opting for the Omnibus Decree now means being taxed in Ticino at 100% of the tables instead of 80%. There is time until the end of 2026 to regularise.
item.content:encoded:
Since January 2026 the Canton of Ticino withholding tax office has been applying the full rate — 100% of tables A, B, C and H — to cross-border commuters who choose the Omnibus Decree mechanism. Until 2025 the same workers were taxed at 80%, as "new cross-border commuters". The communication was made public by OCST, the canton's most representative trade union.
## Who is affected
The measure concerns a specific group, which OCST calls the "old cross-border commuters from the new municipalities". These are workers who:
- worked in Ticino between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023, returning home daily; - have their tax residence in an Italian municipality within 20 km of the border; - live in a municipality that was nevertheless absent from the Canton of Ticino's old list of border municipalities.
It is the last point that makes the difference, and it is the one most often misunderstood. Being within 20 km is not enough: anyone resident in a municipality already on the old list is unaffected by this communication.
## A two-part mechanism
The tax burden on these workers arises from the interaction of two rules, one Swiss and one Italian.
In Switzerland they pay withholding tax, deducted by the employer on the basis of tables — A, B, C and H — that vary with family circumstances. Until 2025 Ticino applied 80% of the ordinary rate to this group, the treatment reserved for "new cross-border commuters".
In Italy, the Omnibus Decree allows workers to opt for a substitute tax equal to 25% of the withholding tax already paid in Switzerland. Adding the two together, the overall burden was broadly in line with that of "classic" old cross-border commuters: those who pay no direct income tax in Italy but are subject to the full rate in Switzerland. ## What changes
The withholding tax office has determined that anyone opting for the Omnibus mechanism is to be taxed in Ticino at 100% of the tables, no longer at 80%. The balance described above breaks down: the full Swiss rate applies, and the Italian share is added on top.
Workers face two options, each with a cost.
**First option, the Omnibus route.** Withholding tax at 100% in Switzerland, plus the Italian substitute tax of 25% calculated on the amount paid in Switzerland.
**Second option, staying at 80%.** The Swiss rate remains reduced, but the worker is classified for all purposes as a "new cross-border commuter", with the Italian filing consequences that follow.
One point deserves to be stated plainly: the "100%" here is the full rate set by the tax tables, not 100% of the salary. What changes is the percentage applied, not the entire wage.
### An example with hypothetical figures
The values below serve only to illustrate how the calculation works. The actual rate depends on the applicable table, the municipality and family circumstances, and should be checked against your own salary certificate.
Assume gross annual income of 60,000 francs and a full withholding tax of 6,000 francs, that is 10% of gross pay.
- Under the Omnibus option, 6,000 francs are paid in Switzerland, to which the Italian substitute tax is added, calculated as 0.25 × 6,000 = 1,500 francs. The total is 7,500 francs. - Staying at 80%, 4,800 francs are paid in Switzerland, but the position must then be handled in Italy under the rules applicable to new cross-border commuters.
The difference therefore depends on your effective rate: there is no single answer that fits everyone. For an estimate of your own case, start with the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator). ## What to do now
There is time until the end of 2026 to regularise your position. The first step is working out which category you fall into, and that requires two concrete pieces of information.
1. **Check your municipality of tax residence.** Being within 20 km of the border is not enough: you need to know whether that municipality appeared on the Canton of Ticino's old list of border municipalities. That is the criterion separating those affected from those who are not. 2. **Reconstruct your periods of work in Ticino between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023**, with evidence of daily return. Contracts, salary certificates and employer attestations are the documents that count.
That done, the choice between the Omnibus option and the 80% rate must be assessed against the figures on your own payslip, not in the abstract: the outcome changes with the applicable table and family circumstances. A tax adviser who regularly handles cross-border cases is the right person for the simulation. OCST provides assistance to its members.
## The underlying issue is political
The situation stems from an ambiguity that has dragged on for years: two countries reading the same group of workers differently. According to OCST the way out is not individual but political — action by the Italian state with Bern to settle the treatment of these workers once and for all.
Until then the choice rests with the individual worker, against a deadline set for the end of 2026. Anyone in the group described above would be well advised not to wait until the final months: reconstructing work periods and documentation takes time.
The [tax return guide](nav:tax-return) may help in weighing up the two filing regimes.
*Source: [ilgiorno.it](https://www.ilgiorno.it/sondrio/cronaca/caso-frontalieri-altre-tasse-0066da70), 25 January 2026, based on the OCST communication.*

## In a nutshell - The railway section between Agno and Ponte Tresa will be suspended from 3 August to 18 August for maintenance work. - The train service will be replaced by a bus service.
## Key facts - Who: Ferrovie Luganesi SA (FLP) - What: maintenance and renewal work - Where: railway route between Agno and Ponte Tresa - When: August 3 - August 18 - Why: Perform major maintenance and renovation work
The railway section between Agno and Ponte Tresa will be suspended from 3 August to 18 August for maintenance work. The train service will be replaced by a bus service. The interventions will be carried out mainly in the daytime bands, except for some activities that will be carried out in the nighttime bands.
The president of Ferrovie Luganesi SA (FLP), **Riccardo Rossi**, announced that the interventions will be carried out to guarantee the safety and quality of the railway service. "The work will be carried out with the utmost respect for passengers and the environment," Rossi said.
The interventions will include the renewal of the rails, the replacement of some safety elements and the maintenance of the lighting systems. The work will be carried out by a team of 20 workers, including 5 specialised mechanics.
The railway line between Agno and Ponte Tresa is one of the busiest in the canton of Lugano, with about 10 trains per day.
